{
  "id": "SPEC-RELEASE-CONVERGENCE-002",
  "purpose": "Make release execution converge an immutable intent against exact observable provider state so interruption, lost runner state, and already-present objects cannot cause duplicate mutation, permanent Attempting records, or successful incomplete releases.",
  "scope": "The graph-private provider observation boundary, provider-specific exactness rules, execute and reconcile semantics, release-state and receipt responsibilities, remote tag and GitHub Release correctness, registry artifact verification, error reporting, and boundary tests against real subprocess behavior.",
  "non_goals": [
    "Distributed transactions or rollback of immutable registry publications.",
    "Treating the execution journal, a cache, a receipt, a workflow run, or absence of a recorded error as release authority.",
    "Automatically replacing or deleting an externally observed conflicting object.",
    "Compatibility with the current incomplete-success behavior or local-only reconcile output.",
    "Defining the product target roster or workflow approval policy, which are specified separately."
  ],
  "api_surface": [
    {
      "name": "OperationObservation",
      "signature": "enum OperationObservation { Absent, Incomplete(VerifiedPartialEvidence), Exact(VerifiedExternalEvidence), Conflict(ExternalConflict), Unverifiable(ObservationFailure) }",
      "description": "A closed graph-layer classification returned by observing one graph-private prepared operation against its provider; it preserves absence, a verified exact subset with identified missing work, exact equality, conflict, and inability to verify as different states.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "Provider authentication, authorization, rate limit, malformed output, unsupported client behavior, timeout, or transport failure produces Unverifiable, never Absent.",
        "An object with the intended name/version but different target, bytes, metadata, or an unexpected artifact produces Conflict, never Exact or Incomplete."
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "ReleaseObservationEvidence",
      "signature": "versioned enum ReleaseObservationEvidence { RegistryArtifact { identity, digest, byte_length }, RemoteTag { name, target, annotation_digest }, ForgeRelease { release, lifecycle, asset_roster_digest }, ForgeAsset { release, name, digest, byte_length } }",
      "description": "The provider-neutral model-layer evidence schema used by observation reports and receipts; graph-private observations convert to it only after exact verification.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "Evidence identity does not exactly match its ReleaseOperationId.",
        "Provider stderr, credentials, endpoints, headers, arbitrary strings, or mutable configuration are supplied as durable evidence."
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "observe_prepared",
      "signature": "observe_prepared(capability: &ValidatedReleaseIntent, operation: &ReleaseOperationId) -> OperationObservation",
      "description": "The single graph-private read boundary used before mutation, after mutation, by execute, and by reconcile for every operation role.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "The operation is not part of the validated intent or lacks an exact prepared provider identity.",
        "The provider cannot prove the operation's role-specific equality contract."
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "converge_release",
      "signature": "converge_release(capability, validated_artifact_manifest, state_store, receipt_store, permit) -> ReleaseReceipt",
      "description": "Observes the canonical DAG in order, mutates only Absent operations or the closed missing-work set of Incomplete operations with satisfied observed prerequisites, re-observes postconditions, persists diagnostic state atomically, and returns only after a complete receipt is persisted.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "Any operation is Conflict or Unverifiable.",
        "An Absent or Incomplete operation remains non-Exact after its bounded effect attempt.",
        "Any prerequisite is not Exact in the current convergence pass.",
        "State or receipt persistence fails."
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "reconcile_release",
      "signature": "reconcile_release(capability, validated_artifact_manifest, optional_state) -> ReleaseObservationReport",
      "description": "Performs the same complete external observation pass as execution without ApplyPermit or mutation and reports every exact, absent, incomplete, conflicting, or unverifiable operation.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "Intent, source, artifact, or prepared-input validation fails before provider observation.",
        "The report cannot cover every operation exactly once."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    {
      "id": "AC-001",
      "criterion": "Every operation role has one production observer that returns exactly Absent, Incomplete with a verified exact subset and closed missing-work set, Exact with safe typed evidence, Conflict with a closed reason, or Unverifiable with an actionable transient diagnostic. Execute, reconcile, pre-effect checks, post-effect checks, and interruption recovery call that same observer rather than reconstructing provider semantics in sibling paths. ExternalConflict is a closed graph diagnostic taxonomy; serializable success evidence uses the model-owned role-specific schema.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-002",
      "criterion": "Execution observes every operation in canonical DAG order regardless of whether the optional journal says Pending, Attempting, Published, AlreadySatisfied, Failed, or Blocked. Exact is recorded as satisfied without mutation; Absent or Incomplete mutates only the verified missing work at most once in that invocation and must be Exact on post-effect observation; Conflict or Unverifiable exits nonzero without mutating that operation or any dependent operation.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-003",
      "criterion": "A missing, unreadable, stale, or entirely lost execution-state file cannot widen authority or prevent recovery. A fresh runner given the same immutable intent and artifact manifest observes exact existing objects, skips their mutation, creates only absent objects, and converges to the same result; state remains an atomically persisted diagnostic journal bound to the intent.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-004",
      "criterion": "Graph returns a complete typed observation report and receipt only after every intended operation is observed Exact in the same final pass and a matching receipt is atomically persisted. callisto-cli maps any Pending, Attempting, Failed, Blocked, Absent, Incomplete, Conflict, Unverifiable, missing operation, missing receipt, or receipt-write failure to nonzero exit and renders the incomplete operation and recovery action in text and complete JSON.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-005",
      "criterion": "callisto-model owns a strict versioned ReleaseObservationEvidence and ReleaseReceipt schema recording the intent digest, exact operation roster, role-specific safe identity/digest evidence, and whether each object was newly produced or already present. A graph-owned explicit-path ReleaseReceiptStore is the sole production writer and uses callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write. The receipt is output evidence only: execute and reconcile re-observe providers on every invocation and never accept receipt bytes as proof that an external object still exists or still matches.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-006",
      "criterion": "Registry observation compares each independently uploadable provider artifact with its matching expected RegistryPackage entry in the validated intent-bound artifact manifest: crates.io-compatible publication verifies the .crate checksum, npm verifies the packed tarball integrity or bytes, and PyPI verifies each expected distribution file name and SHA-256. Exact files are prominently reported and never republished; a verified exact subset with missing files is Incomplete and uploads only those missing files; a different digest, unexpected conflicting distribution, or provider response that cannot prove equality is fatal. Publication consumes the validated bytes, and any client that regenerates packaging proves the outgoing payload digest before submission.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-007",
      "criterion": "Graph's one observer delegates remote tag resolution, annotated-content comparison, push, and post-push observation to canonical callisto-vcs GitDataSource/GitAccess operations rather than a sibling raw-git protocol. The configured remote must prove the exact tag name resolves to the intended source commit and annotation digest; a matching local-only tag is neither Exact nor post-push confirmation, and a conflicting remote tag is fatal before any forge or asset operation becomes eligible.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-008",
      "criterion": "GitHub Release observation uses supported GitHub CLI or API arguments, classifies the real nonzero-exit HTTP 404 contract as Absent, preserves 401, 403, 429, 5xx, malformed, and transport results as Unverifiable, and proves release identity through the separately verified remote tag rather than target_commitish. ForgePrepare is Exact for the matching draft or its matching published successor and does not require future assets; ForgePublish classifies a matching draft or verified exact subset of assets as Incomplete and is Exact only when the release is published with the complete verified asset roster.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-009",
      "criterion": "GitHub asset observation addresses the exact ProductReleaseId and slot file name, downloads or queries immutable digest-capable data, and proves byte length and SHA-256 against the artifact manifest. An existing same-name asset with a different or unverifiable digest is fatal and is never overwritten; after an upload, the asset is re-observed as Exact before completion.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-010",
      "criterion": "Graph reconciliation is structurally read-only and returns a complete typed report for every operation, not merely a list of locally eligible Pending entries. It requires no ApplyPermit and invokes no registry publish, Git push, GitHub creation, or upload route. callisto-cli preserves the full report in JSON and exits nonzero when the intended release is not completely Exact.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-011",
      "criterion": "Boundary tests exercise realistic subprocess contracts: real Git with a bare remote for absent, exact, and conflicting tags; argv parsing compatible with the installed gh CLI; gh HTTP 404 with its real nonzero exit; 401, 403, 429, and 5xx failures; and local HTTP registry fixtures for absent, exact, conflicting, and unverifiable artifact metadata. An argv-insensitive fake or exit-zero 404 alone cannot satisfy this criterion.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-012",
      "criterion": "Interruption tests stop at each boundary between attempt persistence, each independently uploadable provider artifact, provider success, post-effect observation, terminal-state persistence, and receipt persistence, then resume with both the same journal and no journal on a fresh runner. Every case either uploads only verified missing work and converges without repeating an Exact effect or exits nonzero for Conflict/Unverifiable; no case can return successful incomplete state.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-013",
      "criterion": "The graph-private prepared operation remains the only effect and observation input. Raw artifact manifests are accepted only by a graph validation constructor that returns a non-serializable ValidatedArtifactManifest bound to the same ValidatedReleaseIntent; converge_release accepts only that capability. Provider adapters cannot accept free-form package, version, endpoint, tag, repository, asset name, or digest values from CLI flags, workflow environment, mutable configuration, or execution state after validation.",
      "is_error_case": true
    }
  ],
  "linked_requirement": "REQ-DRAFT-RELEASE-RECOVERY",
  "linked_research": "RESEARCH-RELEASE-MODELS",
  "spec_file_path": "docs/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-CONVERGENCE-002.json",
  "revision_note": "Corrects the local-only, no-automatic-retry recovery semantics in the draft .claude release execution specifications. External state is authoritative for convergence; the journal is not.",
  "reasoning": "The smallest enforceable seam is between graph-private PreparedOperation data and execution state transition. Exact already-present behavior is defined against intent-bound build artifact digests, because package/version existence alone cannot distinguish a correct prior publish from a versioning mistake."

  "id": "SPEC-RELEASE-CONVERGENCE-002",
  "purpose": "Make release execution converge an immutable intent against exact observable provider state so interruption, lost runner state, and already-present objects cannot cause duplicate mutation, permanent Attempting records, or successful incomplete releases.",
  "scope": "The graph-private provider observation boundary, provider-specific exactness rules, execute and reconcile semantics, release-state and receipt responsibilities, remote tag and GitHub Release correctness, registry artifact verification, error reporting, and boundary tests against real subprocess behavior.",
  "non_goals": [
    "Distributed transactions or rollback of immutable registry publications.",
    "Treating the execution journal, a cache, a receipt, a workflow run, or absence of a recorded error as release authority.",
    "Automatically replacing or deleting an externally observed conflicting object.",
    "Compatibility with the current incomplete-success behavior or local-only reconcile output.",
    "Defining the product target roster or workflow approval policy, which are specified separately."
  ],
  "api_surface": [
    {
      "name": "OperationObservation",
      "signature": "enum OperationObservation { Absent, Incomplete(VerifiedPartialEvidence), Exact(VerifiedExternalEvidence), Conflict(ExternalConflict), Unverifiable(ObservationFailure) }",
      "description": "A closed graph-layer classification returned by observing one graph-private prepared operation against its provider; it preserves absence, a verified exact subset with identified missing work, exact equality, conflict, and inability to verify as different states.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "Provider authentication, authorization, rate limit, malformed output, unsupported client behavior, timeout, or transport failure produces Unverifiable, never Absent.",
        "An object with the intended name/version but different target, bytes, metadata, or an unexpected artifact produces Conflict, never Exact or Incomplete."
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "ReleaseObservationEvidence",
      "signature": "versioned enum ReleaseObservationEvidence { RegistryArtifact { identity, digest, byte_length }, RemoteTag { name, target, annotation_digest }, ForgeRelease { release, lifecycle, asset_roster_digest }, ForgeAsset { release, name, digest, byte_length } }",
      "description": "The provider-neutral model-layer evidence schema used by observation reports and receipts; graph-private observations convert to it only after exact verification.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "Evidence identity does not exactly match its ReleaseOperationId.",
        "Provider stderr, credentials, endpoints, headers, arbitrary strings, or mutable configuration are supplied as durable evidence."
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "observe_prepared",
      "signature": "observe_prepared(capability: &ValidatedReleaseIntent, operation: &ReleaseOperationId) -> OperationObservation",
      "description": "The single graph-private read boundary used before mutation, after mutation, by execute, and by reconcile for every operation role.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "The operation is not part of the validated intent or lacks an exact prepared provider identity.",
        "The provider cannot prove the operation's role-specific equality contract."
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "converge_release",
      "signature": "converge_release(capability, validated_artifact_manifest, state_store, receipt_store, permit) -> ReleaseReceipt",
      "description": "Observes the canonical DAG in order, mutates only Absent operations or the closed missing-work set of Incomplete operations with satisfied observed prerequisites, re-observes postconditions, persists diagnostic state atomically, and returns only after a complete receipt is persisted.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "Any operation is Conflict or Unverifiable.",
        "An Absent or Incomplete operation remains non-Exact after its bounded effect attempt.",
        "Any prerequisite is not Exact in the current convergence pass.",
        "State or receipt persistence fails."
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "reconcile_release",
      "signature": "reconcile_release(capability, validated_artifact_manifest, optional_state) -> ReleaseObservationReport",
      "description": "Performs the same complete external observation pass as execution without ApplyPermit or mutation and reports every exact, absent, incomplete, conflicting, or unverifiable operation.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "Intent, source, artifact, or prepared-input validation fails before provider observation.",
        "The report cannot cover every operation exactly once."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    {
      "id": "AC-001",
      "criterion": "Every operation role has one production observer that returns exactly Absent, Incomplete with a verified exact subset and closed missing-work set, Exact with safe typed evidence, Conflict with a closed reason, or Unverifiable with an actionable transient diagnostic. Execute, reconcile, pre-effect checks, post-effect checks, and interruption recovery call that same observer rather than reconstructing provider semantics in sibling paths. ExternalConflict is a closed graph diagnostic taxonomy; serializable success evidence uses the model-owned role-specific schema.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-002",
      "criterion": "Execution observes every operation in canonical DAG order regardless of whether the optional journal says Pending, Attempting, Published, AlreadySatisfied, Failed, or Blocked. Exact is recorded as satisfied without mutation; Absent or Incomplete mutates only the verified missing work at most once in that invocation and must be Exact on post-effect observation; Conflict or Unverifiable exits nonzero without mutating that operation or any dependent operation.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-003",
      "criterion": "A missing, unreadable, stale, or entirely lost execution-state file cannot widen authority or prevent recovery. A fresh runner given the same immutable intent and artifact manifest observes exact existing objects, skips their mutation, creates only absent objects, and converges to the same result; state remains an atomically persisted diagnostic journal bound to the intent.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-004",
      "criterion": "Graph returns a complete typed observation report and receipt only after every intended operation is observed Exact in the same final pass and a matching receipt is atomically persisted. callisto-cli maps any Pending, Attempting, Failed, Blocked, Absent, Incomplete, Conflict, Unverifiable, missing operation, missing receipt, or receipt-write failure to nonzero exit and renders the incomplete operation and recovery action in text and complete JSON.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-005",
      "criterion": "callisto-model owns a strict versioned ReleaseObservationEvidence and ReleaseReceipt schema recording the intent digest, exact operation roster, role-specific safe identity/digest evidence, and whether each object was newly produced or already present. A graph-owned explicit-path ReleaseReceiptStore is the sole production writer and uses callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write. The receipt is output evidence only: execute and reconcile re-observe providers on every invocation and never accept receipt bytes as proof that an external object still exists or still matches.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-006",
      "criterion": "Registry observation compares each independently uploadable provider artifact with its matching expected RegistryPackage entry in the validated intent-bound artifact manifest: crates.io-compatible publication verifies the .crate checksum, npm verifies the packed tarball integrity or bytes, and PyPI verifies each expected distribution file name and SHA-256. Exact files are prominently reported and never republished; a verified exact subset with missing files is Incomplete and uploads only those missing files; a different digest, unexpected conflicting distribution, or provider response that cannot prove equality is fatal. Publication consumes the validated bytes, and any client that regenerates packaging proves the outgoing payload digest before submission.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-007",
      "criterion": "Graph's one observer delegates remote tag resolution, annotated-content comparison, push, and post-push observation to canonical callisto-vcs GitDataSource/GitAccess operations rather than a sibling raw-git protocol. The configured remote must prove the exact tag name resolves to the intended source commit and annotation digest; a matching local-only tag is neither Exact nor post-push confirmation, and a conflicting remote tag is fatal before any forge or asset operation becomes eligible.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-008",
      "criterion": "GitHub Release observation uses supported GitHub CLI or API arguments, classifies the real nonzero-exit HTTP 404 contract as Absent, preserves 401, 403, 429, 5xx, malformed, and transport results as Unverifiable, and proves release identity through the separately verified remote tag rather than target_commitish. ForgePrepare is Exact for the matching draft or its matching published successor and does not require future assets; ForgePublish classifies a matching draft or verified exact subset of assets as Incomplete and is Exact only when the release is published with the complete verified asset roster.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-009",
      "criterion": "GitHub asset observation addresses the exact ProductReleaseId and slot file name, downloads or queries immutable digest-capable data, and proves byte length and SHA-256 against the artifact manifest. An existing same-name asset with a different or unverifiable digest is fatal and is never overwritten; after an upload, the asset is re-observed as Exact before completion.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-010",
      "criterion": "Graph reconciliation is structurally read-only and returns a complete typed report for every operation, not merely a list of locally eligible Pending entries. It requires no ApplyPermit and invokes no registry publish, Git push, GitHub creation, or upload route. callisto-cli preserves the full report in JSON and exits nonzero when the intended release is not completely Exact.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-011",
      "criterion": "Boundary tests exercise realistic subprocess contracts: real Git with a bare remote for absent, exact, and conflicting tags; argv parsing compatible with the installed gh CLI; gh HTTP 404 with its real nonzero exit; 401, 403, 429, and 5xx failures; and local HTTP registry fixtures for absent, exact, conflicting, and unverifiable artifact metadata. An argv-insensitive fake or exit-zero 404 alone cannot satisfy this criterion.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-012",
      "criterion": "Interruption tests stop at each boundary between attempt persistence, each independently uploadable provider artifact, provider success, post-effect observation, terminal-state persistence, and receipt persistence, then resume with both the same journal and no journal on a fresh runner. Every case either uploads only verified missing work and converges without repeating an Exact effect or exits nonzero for Conflict/Unverifiable; no case can return successful incomplete state.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-013",
      "criterion": "The graph-private prepared operation remains the only effect and observation input. Raw artifact manifests are accepted only by a graph validation constructor that returns a non-serializable ValidatedArtifactManifest bound to the same ValidatedReleaseIntent; converge_release accepts only that capability. Provider adapters cannot accept free-form package, version, endpoint, tag, repository, asset name, or digest values from CLI flags, workflow environment, mutable configuration, or execution state after validation.",
      "is_error_case": true
    }
  ],
  "linked_requirement": "REQ-DRAFT-RELEASE-RECOVERY",
  "linked_research": "RESEARCH-RELEASE-MODELS",
  "spec_file_path": "docs/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-CONVERGENCE-002.json",

{
  "id": "SPEC-RELEASE-ORCHESTRATION-003",
  "purpose": "Define a fast, single-approval GitHub workflow that builds and executes the immutable Callisto product release, supports exact historical recovery on fresh runners, and proves the complete path in an isolated rehearsal before production.",
  "scope": "Release pull request authorization, GitHub Actions jobs and permissions, plan and artifact handoffs, four-target build fan-out, manual historical recovery, removal of the Environment approval, staging-rehearsal topology and failpoints, and retirement of superseded pre-v1 release routes.",
  "non_goals": [
    "A second human approval after the release pull request is merged.",
    "Using GitHub Actions cache, runner-local paths, mutable branches, or workflow output booleans as release authority.",
    "Publishing a rehearsal artifact to crates.io, npmjs.com, production PyPI, or the production Callisto GitHub Release namespace.",
    "Apple Developer ID signing or notarization.",
    "Preserving compatibility for pre-v1 release commands, workflow layouts, state files, or per-package GitHub release behavior."
  ],
  "api_surface": [
    {
      "name": "release workflow dispatch inputs",
      "signature": "workflow_dispatch { release_commit?: full CommitSha, source_run_id?: GitHubRunId, intent_digest?: IntentDigest, artifact_manifest_digest?: ArtifactDigest }",
      "description": "An explicit recovery route that either runs the newly merged release commit or retrieves the exact intent and build handoff from a prior run, then independently validates every binding before credentials are exposed.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "A recovery input is partial, malformed, expired, belongs to another repository, or does not bind the exact release commit and intent digest.",
        "The selected commit is not a verified merge of the managed release pull request."
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "release rehearsal workflow",
      "signature": "rehearse-release(release_commit, failpoint?)",
      "description": "A reusable workflow invocation against an isolated GitHub repository and non-production registry endpoints that runs the same planning, build, attestation, execution, observation, and receipt boundaries as production.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "Any production registry endpoint, production tag namespace, or production release repository is selected.",
        "A configured interruption fails to resume on a new job/run and converge."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    {
      "id": "AC-001",
      "criterion": "The reviewed managed release pull request merge is the sole human approval event. The production workflow contains no environment-policy job, required-reviewer API check, protected Environment reviewer gate, or second manual approval; merge automatically proceeds through plan, build, attest, execute, and final verify when checks pass.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-002",
      "criterion": "The automatic path proves that the triggering commit is exactly one verified merge of the canonical managed release branch, then invokes the provider-neutral callisto release planner to derive and validate the immutable intent from that merge and its reviewed decision. Workflow verifies eligibility and transports files but never constructs operations, tags, package rosters, targets, or artifact names; direct pushes, unrelated pull requests, ambiguous merges, mutable branch tips, and mismatched intent/source fail.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-003",
      "criterion": "Planning has read-only repository permission and no release credentials. Build jobs have only source-read plus attestation/OIDC permissions. A separate read-only validation job validates the intent, source commit, complete artifact manifest, bytes, checksums, and attestations before execute starts. The execute job has job-scoped contents-write permission, repeats validation, and exposes registry secrets only to the final CLI invocation. Removing the Environment gate does not widen any earlier job's permissions.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-004",
      "criterion": "The build stage obtains a total matrix from the CLI's validated immutable intent and maps every declared slot exactly once; an unknown, missing, extra, or workflow-defaulted slot fails before build. It produces the aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, aarch64-unknown-linux-musl, and wasm32-wasip1 payloads plus all registry-package artifacts. A fan-in job validates the complete slot roster, creates deterministic archives and SHA256SUMS, records the artifact manifest, and ensures each required file has a GitHub attestation before execution can start.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-005",
      "criterion": "Intent, artifact-manifest, metadata, and receipt handoffs use strict model schemas, while payload/checksum bytes are validated by those schemas; all are downloaded outside the trusted source checkout and retained for a documented recovery window of at least seven days. Retention grants no authority: CLI revalidates every byte and identifier against the immutable intent, source commit, and original artifact-manifest digest. After expiry, a rebuild is usable only if it reproduces every original digest; otherwise recovery fails with an unrecoverable-handoff diagnostic rather than minting replacement expected bytes.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-006",
      "criterion": "A workflow_dispatch recovery can name an exact historical full release commit and either reproduce the original artifact-manifest digests or consume a named prior run whose intent and artifact-manifest digests are supplied. It verifies the original managed-PR merge, plan digest, source commit, artifact bindings, and original artifact identity, then uses external-state convergence; it never substitutes current main, latest, a different run's artifacts, newly chosen expected bytes, or runner-local state.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-007",
      "criterion": "The execute job invokes the core CLI once with the exact intent, artifact manifest, artifact directory, state path, and receipt path. Workflow shell does not publish registries, derive tag names, create releases, upload product assets, classify already-present responses, or decide completion independently of the CLI.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-008",
      "criterion": "The release workflow fails unless the CLI emits and the workflow validates a complete receipt for the same intent digest. The receipt and complete observation report are uploaded even on failure when safely available; a green execute or workflow conclusion without a valid complete receipt is impossible.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-009",
      "criterion": "The isolated rehearsal uses a dedicated non-production GitHub repository or equivalent isolated forge namespace plus non-production Cargo, npm, and PyPI registry endpoints and credentials. Repository and endpoint selection is resolved by graph before intent derivation and captured in typed intent/prepared bindings; workflow allowlists credentials and environment but cannot override those identities afterward. Allowlists fail closed before production registries, the production repository, or a production callisto@X.Y.Z tag can be addressed.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-010",
      "criterion": "One rehearsal covers managed release-PR merge, immutable plan, every real Callisto registry artifact build, all four product builds and native/WASM smoke tests, checksums, GitHub attestations, product tag, prepared release, asset uploads, final release publication, final observation, and receipt without production credentials. Separate representative npm and PyPI fixtures run through the same production adapters, including per-file interruption, exact rerun, digest conflict, and unverifiable-metadata cases even though Callisto itself currently publishes only Cargo packages.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-011",
      "criterion": "Rehearsal failpoints can stop after each provider mutation and before each following journal or receipt write. Each failpoint is resumed in a fresh job or run without its predecessor's RUNNER_TEMP state, and the second run must converge without duplicate mutation or false success. Conflict, unverifiable, expired-handoff, and wrong-source negative cases must also fail with actionable diagnostics.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-012",
      "criterion": "A proposed release-boundary implementation may be developed only in the isolated branch/rehearsal path and cannot be activated against production or used for the first production release until that exact candidate revision passes the full rehearsal suite. Later changes to release intent schemas, provider adapters, operation DAG, build matrix, attestation policy, or workflow handoff contract rerun the rehearsal gate before production activation.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-013",
      "criterion": "Superseded pre-v1 effect routes `plan-publish`, `publish`, `tag --plan`, and `filter-plan` are removed as independent release paths, along with their contradictory documentation. The `version`, changeset, status, matrix, and other non-effect capabilities required to prepare the release pull request remain. Any retained preview delegates to the canonical release planner and cannot publish, tag, upload, or create a release. There is one release plan/inspect/reconcile/execute family, one release-PR action, and one product-release workflow, with no Environment-gated, journal-authoritative, per-package GitHub release, or shell-owned effect path.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-014",
      "criterion": "All third-party Actions remain pinned to immutable commit SHAs; concurrency consumes a CLI-validated canonical ProductReleaseId and repository identity rather than reconstructing a tag in YAML; logs and uploaded diagnostics contain no credentials; and every shell interpolation crossing from workflow inputs is passed through a named environment variable and validated before use.",
      "is_error_case": true
    }
  ],
  "linked_requirement": "REQ-DRAFT-RELEASE-RECOVERY",
  "linked_research": "RESEARCH-RELEASE-MODELS",
  "spec_file_path": "docs/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-ORCHESTRATION-003.json",
  "revision_note": "Supersedes the required-reviewer Environment and compatibility-window criteria in .claude/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-INTERFACES-013.json and related draft release specifications, based on the user's explicit pre-v1 product decisions.",
  "reasoning": "The rehearsal is not another approval gate. It is automated evidence that the same production boundaries work across real job isolation, provider protocols, attestations, and interruption. Thirty-day handoff retention supports recovery while the core still treats only the validated intent, artifact bytes, and observed provider state as authority."
}

  "id": "SPEC-RELEASE-ORCHESTRATION-003",
  "purpose": "Define a fast, single-approval GitHub workflow that builds and executes the immutable Callisto product release, supports exact historical recovery on fresh runners, and proves the complete path in an isolated rehearsal before production.",
  "scope": "Release pull request authorization, GitHub Actions jobs and permissions, plan and artifact handoffs, four-target build fan-out, manual historical recovery, removal of the Environment approval, staging-rehearsal topology and failpoints, and retirement of superseded pre-v1 release routes.",
  "non_goals": [
    "A second human approval after the release pull request is merged.",
    "Using GitHub Actions cache, runner-local paths, mutable branches, or workflow output booleans as release authority.",
    "Publishing a rehearsal artifact to crates.io, npmjs.com, production PyPI, or the production Callisto GitHub Release namespace.",
    "Apple Developer ID signing or notarization.",
    "Preserving compatibility for pre-v1 release commands, workflow layouts, state files, or per-package GitHub release behavior."
  ],
  "api_surface": [
    {
      "name": "release workflow dispatch inputs",
      "signature": "workflow_dispatch { release_commit?: full CommitSha, source_run_id?: GitHubRunId, intent_digest?: IntentDigest, artifact_manifest_digest?: ArtifactDigest }",
      "description": "An explicit recovery route that either runs the newly merged release commit or retrieves the exact intent and build handoff from a prior run, then independently validates every binding before credentials are exposed.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "A recovery input is partial, malformed, expired, belongs to another repository, or does not bind the exact release commit and intent digest.",
        "The selected commit is not a verified merge of the managed release pull request."
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "release rehearsal workflow",
      "signature": "rehearse-release(release_commit, failpoint?)",
      "description": "A reusable workflow invocation against an isolated GitHub repository and non-production registry endpoints that runs the same planning, build, attestation, execution, observation, and receipt boundaries as production.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "Any production registry endpoint, production tag namespace, or production release repository is selected.",
        "A configured interruption fails to resume on a new job/run and converge."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    {
      "id": "AC-001",
      "criterion": "The reviewed managed release pull request merge is the sole human approval event. The production workflow contains no environment-policy job, required-reviewer API check, protected Environment reviewer gate, or second manual approval; merge automatically proceeds through plan, build, attest, execute, and final verify when checks pass.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-002",
      "criterion": "The automatic path proves that the triggering commit is exactly one verified merge of the canonical managed release branch, then invokes the provider-neutral callisto release planner to derive and validate the immutable intent from that merge and its reviewed decision. Workflow verifies eligibility and transports files but never constructs operations, tags, package rosters, targets, or artifact names; direct pushes, unrelated pull requests, ambiguous merges, mutable branch tips, and mismatched intent/source fail.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-003",
      "criterion": "Planning has read-only repository permission and no release credentials. Build jobs have only source-read plus attestation/OIDC permissions. A separate read-only validation job validates the intent, source commit, complete artifact manifest, bytes, checksums, and attestations before execute starts. The execute job has job-scoped contents-write permission, repeats validation, and exposes registry secrets only to the final CLI invocation. Removing the Environment gate does not widen any earlier job's permissions.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-004",
      "criterion": "The build stage obtains a total matrix from the CLI's validated immutable intent and maps every declared slot exactly once; an unknown, missing, extra, or workflow-defaulted slot fails before build. It produces the aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, aarch64-unknown-linux-musl, and wasm32-wasip1 payloads plus all registry-package artifacts. A fan-in job validates the complete slot roster, creates deterministic archives and SHA256SUMS, records the artifact manifest, and ensures each required file has a GitHub attestation before execution can start.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-005",
      "criterion": "Intent, artifact-manifest, metadata, and receipt handoffs use strict model schemas, while payload/checksum bytes are validated by those schemas; all are downloaded outside the trusted source checkout and retained for a documented recovery window of at least seven days. Retention grants no authority: CLI revalidates every byte and identifier against the immutable intent, source commit, and original artifact-manifest digest. After expiry, a rebuild is usable only if it reproduces every original digest; otherwise recovery fails with an unrecoverable-handoff diagnostic rather than minting replacement expected bytes.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-006",
      "criterion": "A workflow_dispatch recovery can name an exact historical full release commit and either reproduce the original artifact-manifest digests or consume a named prior run whose intent and artifact-manifest digests are supplied. It verifies the original managed-PR merge, plan digest, source commit, artifact bindings, and original artifact identity, then uses external-state convergence; it never substitutes current main, latest, a different run's artifacts, newly chosen expected bytes, or runner-local state.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-007",
      "criterion": "The execute job invokes the core CLI once with the exact intent, artifact manifest, artifact directory, state path, and receipt path.       "is_error_case": true

      "criterion": "The isolated rehearsal uses a dedicated non-production GitHub repository or equivalent isolated forge namespace plus non-production Cargo, npm, and PyPI registry endpoints and credentials. Allowlists fail closed before production registries, the production repository, or a production callisto@X.Y.Z tag can be addressed.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-010",
      "criterion": "One rehearsal covers managed release-PR merge, immutable plan, every real Callisto registry artifact build, all four product builds and native/WASM smoke tests, checksums, GitHub attestations, product tag, prepared release, asset uploads, final release publication, final observation, and receipt without production credentials.       "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-011",
      "criterion": "Rehearsal failpoints can stop after each provider mutation and before each following journal or receipt write. Conflict, unverifiable, expired-handoff, and wrong-source negative cases must also fail with actionable diagnostics.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-012",
      "criterion": "A proposed release-boundary implementation may be developed only in the isolated branch/rehearsal path and cannot be activated against production or used for the first production release until that exact candidate revision passes the full rehearsal suite. Later changes to release intent schemas, provider adapters, operation DAG, build matrix, attestation policy, or workflow handoff contract rerun the rehearsal gate before production activation.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-013",
      "criterion": "Superseded pre-v1 effect routes `plan-publish`, `publish`, `tag --plan`, and `filter-plan` are removed as independent release paths, along with their contradictory documentation. The `version`, changeset, status, matrix, and other non-effect capabilities required to prepare the release pull request remain. Any retained preview delegates to the canonical release planner and cannot publish, tag, upload, or create a release. There is one release plan/inspect/reconcile/execute family, one release-PR action, and one product-release workflow, with no Environment-gated, journal-authoritative, per-package GitHub release, or shell-owned effect path.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-014",
      "criterion": "All third-party Actions remain pinned to immutable commit SHAs; concurrency consumes a CLI-validated canonical ProductReleaseId and repository identity rather than reconstructing a tag in YAML; logs and uploaded diagnostics contain no credentials; and every shell interpolation crossing from workflow inputs is passed through a named environment variable and validated before use.",
      "is_error_case": true
    }
  ],

  "reasoning": "The rehearsal is not another approval gate. {
  "id": "SPEC-RELEASE-ORCHESTRATION-003",
  "purpose": "Define a fast, single-approval GitHub workflow that builds and executes the immutable Callisto product release, supports exact historical recovery on fresh runners, and proves the complete path in an isolated rehearsal before production.",
  "scope": "Release pull request authorization, GitHub Actions jobs and permissions, plan and artifact handoffs, four-target build fan-out, manual historical recovery, removal of the Environment approval, staging-rehearsal topology and failpoints, and retirement of superseded pre-v1 release routes.",
  "non_goals": [
    "A second human approval after the release pull request is merged.",
    "Using GitHub Actions cache, runner-local paths, mutable branches, or workflow output booleans as release authority.",
    "Publishing a rehearsal artifact to crates.io, npmjs.com, production PyPI, or the production Callisto GitHub Release namespace.",
    "Apple Developer ID signing or notarization.",
    "Preserving compatibility for pre-v1 release commands, workflow layouts, state files, or per-package GitHub release behavior."
  ],
  "api_surface": [
    {
      "name": "release workflow dispatch inputs",
      "signature": "workflow_dispatch { release_commit?: full CommitSha, source_run_id?: GitHubRunId, intent_digest?: IntentDigest, artifact_manifest_digest?: ArtifactDigest }",
      "description": "An explicit recovery route that either runs the newly merged release commit or retrieves the exact intent and build handoff from a prior run, then independently validates every binding before credentials are exposed.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "A recovery input is partial, malformed, expired, belongs to another repository, or does not bind the exact release commit and intent digest.",
        "The selected commit is not a verified merge of the managed release pull request."
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "release rehearsal workflow",
      "signature": "rehearse-release(release_commit, failpoint?)",
      "description": "A reusable workflow invocation against an isolated GitHub repository and non-production registry endpoints that runs the same planning, build, attestation, execution, observation, and receipt boundaries as production.",
      "error_conditions": [
        "Any production registry endpoint, production tag namespace, or production release repository is selected.",
        "A configured interruption fails to resume on a new job/run and converge."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    {
      "id": "AC-001",
      "criterion": "The reviewed managed release pull request merge is the sole human approval event. The production workflow contains no environment-policy job, required-reviewer API check, protected Environment reviewer gate, or second manual approval; merge automatically proceeds through plan, build, attest, execute, and final verify when checks pass.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-002",
      "criterion": "The automatic path proves that the triggering commit is exactly one verified merge of the canonical managed release branch, then invokes the provider-neutral callisto release planner to derive and validate the immutable intent from that merge and its reviewed decision. Workflow verifies eligibility and transports files but never constructs operations, tags, package rosters, targets, or artifact names; direct pushes, unrelated pull requests, ambiguous merges, mutable branch tips, and mismatched intent/source fail.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-003",
      "criterion": "Planning has read-only repository permission and no release credentials. Build jobs have only source-read plus attestation/OIDC permissions. A separate read-only validation job validates the intent, source commit, complete artifact manifest, bytes, checksums, and attestations before execute starts. The execute job has job-scoped contents-write permission, repeats validation, and exposes registry secrets only to the final CLI invocation. Removing the Environment gate does not widen any earlier job's permissions.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-004",
      "criterion": "The build stage obtains a total matrix from the CLI's validated immutable intent and maps every declared slot exactly once; an unknown, missing, extra, or workflow-defaulted slot fails before build. It produces the aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, aarch64-unknown-linux-musl, and wasm32-wasip1 payloads plus all registry-package artifacts. A fan-in job validates the complete slot roster, creates deterministic archives and SHA256SUMS, records the artifact manifest, and ensures each required file has a GitHub attestation before execution can start.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-005",
      "criterion": "Intent, artifact-manifest, metadata, and receipt handoffs use strict model schemas, while payload/checksum bytes are validated by those schemas; all are downloaded outside the trusted source checkout and retained for a documented recovery window of at least seven days. Retention grants no authority: CLI revalidates every byte and identifier against the immutable intent, source commit, and original artifact-manifest digest. After expiry, a rebuild is usable only if it reproduces every original digest; otherwise recovery fails with an unrecoverable-handoff diagnostic rather than minting replacement expected bytes.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-006",
      "criterion": "A workflow_dispatch recovery can name an exact historical full release commit and either reproduce the original artifact-manifest digests or consume a named prior run whose intent and artifact-manifest digests are supplied. It verifies the original managed-PR merge, plan digest, source commit, artifact bindings, and original artifact identity, then uses external-state convergence; it never substitutes current main, latest, a different run's artifacts, newly chosen expected bytes, or runner-local state.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-007",
      "criterion": "The execute job invokes the core CLI once with the exact intent, artifact manifest, artifact directory, state path, and receipt path. Workflow shell does not publish registries, derive tag names, create releases, upload product assets, classify already-present responses, or decide completion independently of the CLI.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-008",
      "criterion": "The release workflow fails unless the CLI emits and the workflow validates a complete receipt for the same intent digest. The receipt and complete observation report are uploaded even on failure when safely available; a green execute or workflow conclusion without a valid complete receipt is impossible.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-009",
      "criterion": "The isolated rehearsal uses a dedicated non-production GitHub repository or equivalent isolated forge namespace plus non-production Cargo, npm, and PyPI registry endpoints and credentials. Repository and endpoint selection is resolved by graph before intent derivation and captured in typed intent/prepared bindings; workflow allowlists credentials and environment but cannot override those identities afterward. Allowlists fail closed before production registries, the production repository, or a production callisto@X.Y.Z tag can be addressed.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {

content.text:
Recommended challenge verdict: FAIL for all five plans and the program. All five spec hashes match, and every acceptance criterion is listed in at least one task. The blockers are execution ordering, missing implementation ownership, and verification that cannot prove the claimed behavior.

1. Critical — Orchestration duplicates shared authority and depends on convergence that it also proposes to implement.

   `SPEC-RELEASE-ORCHESTRATION-003/T001` adds `ReleaseObservationEvidence`, `ReleaseReceipt`, artifact contracts, and prepared bindings; these already belong to product `PM-001/PM-002` and convergence `T1/T3`. Orchestration `T002` repeats product identity, fixture exclusion, slot derivation, and DAG construction. Its `T003` waits for the entire convergence implementation to pass, then adds the provider adapters and receipt emission that convergence must already have to pass. It also still names `ArtifactManifestV1` after product requires replacing that shape.

   These tasks collide in `callisto-model/src/release.rs` and graph `release.rs`, `release_artifacts.rs`, and `release_execution.rs`. The architecture model explicitly keeps prepared effect authority graph-private and makes `.github` a consumer.

   Correction: make product the sole owner of product/slot derivation, convergence the sole owner of observation/dispatch/receipts, and orchestration the consumer of completed contracts. Reduce orchestration T001–T004 to genuinely orchestration-specific handoffs, historical-run validation, and CLI exposure. Record qualified cross-plan prerequisites in an executable program ordering.

2. Critical — Exact registry publication bytes have no concrete implementation task.

   Product `PM-005` validates artifacts; convergence `T3` observes external bytes and `T4` changes execution order. None specifies replacing the actual packaging/submission seam or proving outgoing bytes before submission. Orchestration `T003` vaguely adds adapters only after convergence is supposed to pass.

   Live evidence: graph `release.rs:370` calls `cargo_publish_argv`, `npm_publish_argv`, and a PyPI build/upload pair. `registry_argv.rs:63` publishes a Cargo manifest; `:196` publishes npm workspaces through npm/pnpm/Yarn/Bun; `:284` rebuilds Python distributions and uploads a glob. Those APIs accept neither validated artifact bytes nor an expected digest.

   Therefore a validated manifest can coexist with publication of newly generated, different bytes. Post-publication observation detects the mistake after an irreversible effect. This leaves product AC-006 and convergence AC-006/013 incomplete.

   Correction: assign convergence an explicit dispatch migration covering Cargo, every npm manager path, and individual PyPI distribution files. Name the helper files and eliminate workspace packaging authority after validation. Test captured outgoing bytes and pre-submission rejection of regenerated mismatches, plus partial PyPI uploads.

3. High — Product and membership batches cannot satisfy their own compilation gates.

   Product `PM-001/PM-002` remove old wire types and package-owned operation fields while downstream callers migrate only in `PM-004/PM-005` and convergence. Yet the first batch runs workspace tests/lints. Existing graph `release_execution.rs:10,40,71,190` imports and constructs `ArtifactManifestV1`/`ArtifactSlotId`; graph `release.rs:395` reads `id.package`. Removing those contracts first breaks these consumers.

   Membership `M-001` changes Cargo/uv readers and the shared glob builder to return `Result`, but `IgnoreWalkLocator` migration is deferred to M-002/M-003. Its existing callers at `locate/ignore_walk.rs:38–40` still consume direct membership values. Existing npm membership construction also calls the same glob builder (`membership.rs:359,364`). M-B1 contains only M-001 but requires `just test` to pass.

   Correction: make breaking signatures and all immediate consumers one compilation transaction. Split nonbreaking preparation separately if useful; do not retain compatibility decoders. Product’s no-orphan dispatch gate also needs task-level ordering with convergence rather than making the entire product plan a prerequisite for code needed to satisfy its gate.

4. High — Required distribution verification is only name-checked.

   Product AC-005 requires macOS ad-hoc signing and local verification, both Linux architecture/static-link checks and native execution, and the real release-profile WASM payload in Moon/Extism. `PM-005` claims this criterion but tests manifest validation. Orchestration `T005/T007` say “native and WASM smoke tests” without assigning codesign/static-link checks or changing the sandbox’s artifact input.

   Live evidence: `crates/callisto-moon/tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs:41` loads `target/wasm32-wasip1/debug/callisto_moon.wasm` and stages a debug fixture at `:90`. Existing `just wasm-check` also builds without `--release`. Passing these gates cannot establish that the shipped WASM file works.

   Correction: assign concrete build validation commands and matching native runners, extend the sandbox to consume the exact release artifact, and bind verification to the final payload digest. Include deliberately wrong architecture, dynamic linkage, unsigned/invalid macOS, and broken release-WASM negatives.

5. High — Fixture classification has no configured representation or complete implementation boundary.

   Product `PM-003` proposes recording a dev-only classification in `callisto.toml`, but only owns that file and `release_decision.rs`. Live `config/raw.rs:5,71,94` denies unknown fields; package configuration exposes `release-trigger`, `publish-to`, etc., with no dev-only release classification. Resolved configuration also has no proposed field.

   The task does not choose whether an existing setting supplies this meaning or add the new raw/resolved field and propagation. Adding an invented key fails configuration loading; merely removing the fixture from a fixed group fails the promised coordinated source-version behavior.

   Correction: specify the exact representation, own raw/resolved configuration and its propagation, and test exclusion from decision authority while preserving source version updates. Prove both explicit selection rejection and that fixtures cannot appear through dependency/prerequisite derivation.

6. High — Setup does not close the existing WASM cache-hit bypass.

   Setup `S-001–S-004` centralize resolution and verification but never assign cache identity/revalidation behavior. Live `setup-callisto-wasm/action.yml:27` keys the cache by unresolved `inputs.version`, and `:31` skips the download step on a cache hit. A literal `latest` cache can remain indefinitely old; replacing only inline download logic with the helper leaves cache hits outside resolution and verification.

   Correction: resolve the immutable identity before lookup and always validate cached bytes/provenance, or remove this cache. Add actual composite-action cache-hit tests for stale `latest`, corrupted exact-version bytes, and wrong metadata. Declare the WASM-specific installed-version verification path explicitly instead of applying a native `callisto --version` expectation indiscriminately.

7. High — Production activation ordering and rehearsal identity are not concretely enforceable.

   Orchestration `T006` installs the automatic production trigger and removes its current gate; the replacement exact-candidate activation gate appears only in `T010`, after rehearsal. Prose says to block activation but does not establish a disabled production entry point before T006 or specify how the exact candidate evidence reaches the enabled workflow. This matters because the first production run must not be the test of the new boundary.

   Additionally, `T007` categorically prohibits a `callisto@X.Y.Z` tag while product `PM-004` necessarily derives exactly that tag. The spec prohibits addressing the production tag namespace, so isolation must be expressed as repository plus tag identity, or a specified staging product identity—not an incompatible standalone tag ban.

   Correction: establish the fail-closed activation mechanism before introducing the automatic trigger; exercise disabled production behavior in a negative test. Define the staging repository/product binding concretely and verify that production credentials and repository targets remain unreachable.

Setup `S-004` says `just ci` includes repository contract tests; the live Justfile’s `ci` dependency list does not include those shell tests.

   Several steps remain “implement the gated contract” without a chosen API or concrete baseline, particularly new remote Git operations and recovery handoffs. That falls short of navigator’s implementation-ready requirement at precisely the changed interfaces.

   Correction: add appropriate task-runner targets, correct crate/test ownership, and wire the new shell suites into persistent CI. State the selected API signatures and integration points rather than requiring implementers to design them during execution.
